title: 把伺服器開機從幾小時縮到幾分鐘——Cloudflare 拆 UEFI、iPXE、firmware 三層遲延
summary: Cloudflare core 團隊把一台 Gen12 server 的 firmware 升級重開時間從近 4 小時壓到 3 分鐘——把延遲拆成 UEFI HII lazy-load、iPXE 四段 network-boot timeout、CfHIIConfig_App regex + hex-equal skip 三層分別治根。
widget_questions: Which sub-layer of the boot stack (UEFI HII lazy-load, iPXE four-attempt timeout chain, CfHIIConfig_App R-M-W loop, vendor NIC string mismatch) owns each chunk of the 4-hour-to-3-minute delta, and what assumption originally made that layer slow?

Where exactly did the 4-hour firmware-upgrade budget actually go — and after the fix, how does the per-line minute count change between iPXE timeouts, HII recompute, BMC self-init, CfHIIConfig R-M-W, vendor-string retries, and serial-console waits?

Why does the same logical 'HTTPS-over-IPv4 boot interface' produce incompatible strings on two different NIC vendors (one carrying OCP SKU, the other a MAC), and how does CfHIIConfig_App's regex pattern collapse them onto one immutable hex-equal NV variable?

Across a fleet of N machines on a quarterly firmware-update cadence, how does the per-machine 19-minute boot saving compound into annual wall-clock — and at what fleet size does the engineering cost of the dig-and-fix become self-justifying?
